newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Unidare expects growth, seeks acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Unidare expects growth, seeks acquisitions.

text.p: Irish engineering company Unidare said on Monday it expected to bounce back from this year's fall in profits as its disposals programme and capital investment programme began to bear fruit.
"Following the disposals programme, Unidare now has a narrower and more focused portfolio of businesses from which we expect to grow," Unidare said in a results statement.
"Despite an uncertain outlook in many of our markets, we expect that recent management initiatives and our capital investment programme will begin to bear fruit this year," the statement said.

But Unidare warned that the recent strength of the Irish pound would, if sustained, adversely impact the translation of profits generated this year in its U.S. and Dutch operations although this would be partially offset if sterling's relative strength continued.

The company announced a drop in pre-tax profits to 4.44 million Irish pounds for the year ended September 30 compared to 8.14 million in 1995. An exceptional charge of 1.43 million was incurred in relation to disposals.

It said it had approved capital expenditure of 3.2 million Irish pounds for the current year and that resources would be devoted to the search for acquisitions with clear linkages with its two core divisions.
"Our ungeared balance sheet provides the platform to actively pursue profitable growth opportunities," Unidare said.
"We are strengthening businesses by investing in people and capital projects designed to enhance capacity, quality and efficiency across all of our chosen operations," it added.
The company said its engineering supplies distribution division had a difficult year with operating profits falling to 3.7 million Irish pounds from 5.7 million.
"The performance in the USA and Europe both fell well behind expectations, reflecting difficult market conditions and margin pressure," the statement said.
Unidare said it had effected management changes and developed new value-added services to strengthen customer relations.
A two million Irish pound investment had been sanctioned in new computer and telecommunications systems to improve service and reduce transaction costs and working capital investments, it added.
Unidare's division manufacturing specialised engineering products recorded higher operating profits of 3.0 million Irish pounds compared with 2.6 million the previous year.
The company said its disposal programme, mostly carried out in the last two years, had realised 18 million Irish pounds.

"The strategy was to recover capital invested in businesses where, for Unidare, the outlook was poor and to re-invest this capital in the business where there were opportunities for long-term growth and acceptable returns," the statement said.
Unidare said it now has the distribution of engineering supplies and the manufacture of specialised engineering products as its two core divisions.
